reasons.dead|aside.atlas-layers: The layer rail is a floating panel ON the map, not a column beside it. It is short on purpose — a rail as tall as the map would cover the city — so the space under it is the map itself. Check it: open /atlas at 1440px; the rail is 74x26 at x=12, y=62..88, and the element under it at 40, 150, 300, 450 and 600px below is canvas.maplibregl-canvas — satellite imagery and 3D blocks, not an empty band. The gate measures that space at 726..882px across the sweep, in a row of 818..974px. It is the map: the product, not a gap.
reasons.wrap|div.atlas-page-tools: Below 340px the three page-level doors (city watch, Research & method, Data & sources) cannot sit on one row beside the Layers button: they need about 355px at the tightest padding that keeps them legible, and a 320px phone has 320. They wrap, and Data & sources ends up alone on the second row, right-aligned under the others. The alternative is the one that shipped until 22 October 2026: the row ran under Layers and hid its "+". A second short row over the map costs a few lines of city; a button covered by its neighbour costs a door. Check it: open /atlas at 339px and see City watch and Research & method on one row, Data & sources below them, and Layers uncovered. Wider than 340px the row is single and this reason does not apply.
reasons.dead|div.atlas-page-tools: The three page-level doors — City watch, Research & method, Data & sources — are one right-hand row floating over the map, not a column beside it. The row is 30px tall because each door is a closed disclosure that opens over the map rather than taking a column of its own, so the map keeps every pixel of its height. Check it: open /atlas at 1440px; the row is 306x30 at x=1126, y=62..92, and the element under it at 40, 150, 300, 450 and 600px below is canvas.maplibregl-canvas. The gate measures that space at 689..936px across the sweep, in a row of 818..974px. It is the map.
